Picture: Replicas of Prehistoric Tools. The picture shows several pointed stone tools, including blades and arrowhead-like pieces, and tools with wooden handles attached to stone heads.
In social studies class, students are learning about the different tools made by early humans in prehistoric times.
Describe the types of tools in this picture and what they could have been used for.
Compare the tools that we use today to tools used back then. Explain the differences and similarities you see.
Describe what life might have been like during prehistoric times. Use as many details as you can.

Four pictures in order: 1. Two young people put on outer clothing near a doorway. 2. They walk along a sidewalk; paper money is falling behind one of them. 3. Inside a shop with goods on shelves, one person checks their pockets while the other holds a shopping basket and looks back. 4. One person runs back along the sidewalk toward paper money lying on the ground.
Look at the pictures. Use the pictures to write a story. Your story should have a beginning, a middle, and an end. Write about each picture in order. Include as many details as you can.
Tell who the people are, where they went, what they did, and why.
Explain what the people saw, what they said, and how they felt.

Think about the foods you most like to eat.
What are five of your favorite foods? Why do you like these foods?
Would you rather have to eat only these five foods every day for a month or not eat any of these five foods for a month? Explain your decision.
28:
Stimulus: A line graph titled "Number of Vehicles in the United States (millions)". The x-axis is Year (2016, 2017, 2018, 2019). The y-axis is Number of Vehicles (millions), with labeled ticks from 264 to 280 in increments of 2. Red points connected by straight red lines are labeled: 2016: 268.8; 2017: 272.5; 2018: 273.6; 2019: 276.5.
Describe this line graph. What conclusions can you make from the data shown?
In which year did the number of vehicles in the United States grow the most? How do you know?
Based on this graph, explain two things you think will happen in the next five years.
